title: Critical Swendsen–Wang spectral-gap exponent
formal: For critical two-state Swendsen–Wang dynamics on square tori, does z=lim_{L→∞} log(1/gap(P_L))/log L exist, and if it does, determine z?
definitions: For integer L≥3, the square torus has vertices (Z/LZ)^2 and an undirected edge between vertices differing by 1 or −1 in exactly one coordinate and agreeing in the other; duplicate edges are suppressed. A q-state spin configuration assigns a color in {1,…,q} to each vertex. At inverse temperature β, μ(σ)=Z^(−1)exp(β∑_{uv∈E}1[σ(u)=σ(v)]), with no external field. A Swendsen–Wang step independently retains each monochromatic edge with probability p=1−exp(−β), retains no other edges, and independently assigns each resulting connected component a uniform color in {1,…,q}. Singletons are components as well. The critical inverse temperature in this normalization is β_c(q)=log(1+sqrt(q)). Here q=2, β=log(1+sqrt 2) and p=sqrt(2)/(1+sqrt 2); equivalently ±1 Ising spins have coupling β_Ising=β/2. The reversible matrix P_L has real eigenvalues 1=λ_1>λ_2≥…; define gap(P_L)=1−λ_2, the ordinary spectral gap, not the absolute-eigenvalue gap. The target concerns one full cluster update. Write z_L=log(1/gap(P_L))/log L for integers L≥3. A positive existence answer means convergence to a finite real number z. If no finite limit exists, a rigorous nonexistence proof is a complete alternative answer; no limit is presumed from a fitted power law.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof either that z_L has no finite real limit, or that it converges to a finite z together with a real approximation a satisfying |a−z|≤1/100. In the convergent case this certifies 1/gap(P_L)=L^{z+o(1)}; it need not resolve smaller-order factors.
context: Polynomial control of critical Ising dynamics does not identify the precise logarithmic growth exponent of its cluster chain.
why: The dynamic critical exponent measures the intrinsic cost of cluster sampling near a phase transition.
